slides.1.title: Portugal's Five Core Red Grapes
slides.1.items.0.desc: Portugal's most noble variety. Dark, high in tannin, with complex floral aromas. The first choice for Port and the soul of top Douro DOC reds
slides.1.items.1.desc: The most widely planted variety in the Douro. Balanced, elegant structure with red fruit and floral notes, low yields and high quality, often blended with Touriga Nacional
slides.1.items.2.desc: The same as Spain's Tempranillo. Known in Portugal as Aragonez (Alentejo) or Roriz (Douro). Fragrant red fruit, medium tannins
slides.1.items.3.desc: Found across central and southern Portugal. High acidity and colour with spicy character, common in Alentejo blends
slides.1.items.4.desc: The soul variety of Bairrada. Very high acidity and tannin; with age it develops complex notes of leather, earth and dried flowers
slides.2.title: 🍇 Interactive Profiles of the Douro's Five Red Grapes
slides.2.description: Tap Touriga Nacional / Touriga Franca / Tinta Roriz / Trincadeira / Baga for detailed variety profiles: their role in the Douro, structure, aromas and representative wines. Understand why these five varieties are the soul of Portugal's top wines.
slides.3.question: In which region is "Touriga Nacional" mainly planted, forming the core of Port?
slides.3.explanation: Touriga Nacional is Portugal's most noble variety, mainly planted in the Douro Valley. It is one of the most important Port (Porto) varieties and the soul of top Douro DOC reds.
slides.4.question: In the "douro-grapes" variety profiles, Portugal's "Tinta Roriz / Aragonez" is the same grape as which Spanish variety?
slides.4.explanation: Tinta Roriz (the Douro name) and Aragonez (the Alentejo name) are both Portuguese names for Spain's Tempranillo. It is one of the Iberian Peninsula's most important shared varieties, contributing structure and ageing capacity in the Douro and abundant fruit and soft tannins in Alentejo.

slides.5.keyPoints.0: Touriga Nacional: Portugal's most noble variety, dark and floral, the core of Port
slides.5.keyPoints.1: Touriga Franca: the most planted in the Douro, elegant and balanced
slides.5.keyPoints.2: Tinta Roriz / Aragonez: the same as Spain's Tempranillo
slides.5.keyPoints.3: Trincadeira: high acidity and deep colour, found across the south
slides.5.keyPoints.4: Baga: the soul of Bairrada, high in acidity and tannin, ages well
